To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the real yields on Argentine indexed bonds were lower than real interest rates in the U.S. and other countries; (2) the real yields were lower than the expected inflation rate in Argentina; and (3) the real yields and the expected inflation rate moved together in the same direction.

the real interest rates on the indexed bonds in the Argentine economy were significantly lower than those on the unindexed bonds, that expected inflation is an important determinant of the real interest rates in this economy and that the real interest rate on the indexed bond is a good proxy for the expected real interest rate in the economy.

the real yields on Argentine indexed bonds were negatively related to expected inflation and that this relation was stronger when expected inflation was high and when the real yield on indexed bonds was low.
